sections.h2: What roof work looks like in a newer community
sections.body:
Eastmark held its grand opening in June 2013 on the old GM Proving Grounds, and builders kept adding neighborhoods for years afterward. Landsea Homes opened Greenpointe at Eastmark in late 2021. So nearly every roof here is in its first decade or two of service.

Pitched concrete tile is the standard for Phoenix-area production homes built in this period, and we expect to see it on most Eastmark houses, though we confirm what is actually on your home at every visit. A young tile roof seldom needs replacing. What it does need is attention to small problems: a tile cracked by foot traffic, a vent boot drying out in the sun, or a valley packed with leaves and dust.

sections.h2: Monsoon storms and newer tile roofs
sections.body:
Arizona's monsoon season runs June 15–September 30. Storms that cross the open land of the southeast Valley can carry strong gusts, and those gusts can lift ridge caps and edge tiles even on a roof that is only a few years old. Wind-driven rain then finds openings that a calm shower would never reach.

After a big storm, walk the perimeter of your house. Look for tile pieces in the yard, ridge caps that look out of line, and new stains on ceilings or around skylights. If you spot any of these, have the roof looked at before the next storm arrives. Our storm and damaged roof page explains what we check.

sections.h2: Solar mounts and other roof penetrations
sections.body:
Plenty of newer homes add solar after move-in. Each mount that passes through tile is a place where water can enter if the flashing is not done well, and tiles sometimes crack while crews walk the roof during installation.

If a leak shows up after a solar install, or you notice broken tiles near the array, we can inspect and repair the roofing around it. We do not install solar panels; our job is the roof underneath them. The same goes for satellite dishes, added vents and anything else that has been fastened through the roof since the house was built.

If your house is only a few years old, check your builder paperwork before calling anyone. Some workmanship items may be the builder's responsibility, and that is between you and your builder.

Eastmark is an HOA community, and most HOAs require architectural approval for exterior changes such as a different tile color or profile. Repairs using matching tile usually raise no questions, but confirm with your HOA before any work that changes how the roof looks from the street. We are happy to provide product details for your application.

Concrete tile itself lasts a very long time. The underlayment beneath it is the layer that actually keeps water out, and in Arizona heat traditional felt often lasts about 20–25 years. Newer synthetic underlayments can last longer.

For an Eastmark home built in 2013, that means the first wave of underlayment work is likely to start in the 2030s. A roof inspection every few years lets you budget for it on your schedule instead of after a ceiling stain. When the time comes, a tile re-felt usually lets us reuse sound tiles.

sections.h2: Habits that help a young roof last
sections.body: A few simple habits go a long way on a newer home.
bullets: Keep people off the tile unless they know where to step; most cracked tiles we see were stepped on.
Clear valleys, gutters and roof drains before monsoon season starts.
Trim trees so branches do not rub or drop debris onto the roof.
Check the attic or ceilings after heavy rain for fresh stains.
Keep a simple file of any roof repairs, solar work and inspection reports for resale.

faqs: Do Eastmark homes need a new roof yet?

Most do not. Homes here date from 2013 onward, so the tile and underlayment on most houses are still within their expected service life. The work we usually expect in a community this young is repair: cracked tiles, flashing, vents and storm damage.
What kind of roof do most Eastmark homes have?

Concrete tile on pitched roofs is typical for Phoenix-area production homes built since 2013, so it is what we expect to find on most Eastmark houses. We have not seen a community-wide source confirming it, so we always check the actual roof during an estimate.
Should I call my builder or a roofer about a leak?

If your home is new enough that builder paperwork may still apply, start by reading it and contacting the builder about workmanship items. For storm damage, solar-related leaks or homes outside that window, call us at 602-548-3770 and we will set up a visit.
Do I need HOA approval to repair my roof in Eastmark?

Repairs with matching tile usually do not change the look of the home, but rules vary, so check with your HOA first. Anything that changes tile color, profile or material should go through architectural approval before work starts.
Can you fix a leak around my solar panels?

Yes. We repair the tile, flashing and underlayment around solar mounts and other penetrations. We do not install or remove solar equipment, so if panels need to come off for a larger repair, your solar company handles that part.
How often should an Eastmark roof be inspected?
For a newer home, every few years is reasonable, plus a look after any severe monsoon storm. Inspections catch cracked tiles and failing sealant early, while repairs are still small.
Is monsoon wind a real risk for a new tile roof?

It can be. Strong gusts can lift ridge caps and edge tiles on any roof, and a single displaced tile can let wind-driven rain reach the underlayment. Checking the roof after big storms is the best defense.
Do you offer financing for roof work?
Yes, financing is available. Ask about it during your estimate and we will walk you through the options.
What are your office hours?
We are open Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm, and closed Saturday and Sunday. Call 602-548-3770. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

sections.h2: Why late-1990s Las Sendas roofs need a closer look

When the underlayment is worn but the tile is sound, the usual fix is a lift and relay, also called a re-felt. We remove the tile, replace the underlayment and flashings, then reinstall the original tile with new pieces where needed. You keep the look of your home and avoid buying all-new tile.

sections.h2: Start by finding out what is on your roof now
sections.body:
In a community this old, you cannot assume a roof is original. Dobson Ranch has about 5,000 homes built between 1973 and 1999, and over five decades many have been reroofed, added onto or patched by different owners. Valley homes of the 1970s and 1980s commonly had concrete tile or asphalt shingle on pitched roofs, sometimes with flat sections, but we have not verified a community-wide mix.

The first step is to learn what you have: the roof material, when it was last replaced, and what is under it. Purchase disclosures and old permits can help. If there is no paperwork, a roof inspection answers those questions.

sections.h2: Asphalt shingle roofs in west Mesa
sections.body:
Shingles wear faster in Arizona than in cooler climates. Constant UV breaks down the asphalt and the granules that protect it, and summer heat speeds up the process. Signs a shingle roof is near the end include bare spots where granules have washed off, curling or cracked shingles, and granules collecting in gutters.

If your Dobson Ranch home has shingles, regular checks and prompt repair of lifted shingles after monsoon wind help it reach its full life. When it is time, we can replace it. See asphalt shingles for more.

sections.h2: Tile roofs that have reached middle age
sections.body:
On tile homes, the tile itself may be decades old and still serviceable. The underlayment is a different matter. Felt usually lasts about 20–25 years under Arizona tile, so a home from the 1970s or 1980s that has never had a re-felt is well overdue.

A lift and relay replaces the underlayment and flashings and reuses tile that is in good shape. Older tile can be brittle, so we handle it carefully and replace broken pieces with the closest match available.

sections.h2: Flat roofs, additions and patio covers
sections.body:
Older homes often gain a family room, enclosed patio or carport over the years, and those additions are frequently built with low-slope roofs. The joint between an addition and the original roof is one of the most common leak points we see on homes this age.

Foam roofs need recoating every several years, and other flat roof materials need periodic checks of seams and drains. If water ponds on your flat section after a storm, or the surface looks cracked or chalky, see flat roofing and foam roofing.

When a roof has leaked slowly for years, the plywood or plank decking underneath can rot or delaminate. On a reroof of an older Dobson Ranch home, we check the deck as the old materials come off and replace damaged sections before the new roof goes on.

We also look at ventilation. Poor attic airflow makes homes hotter and shortens roof life, and older homes sometimes have fewer vents than current practice calls for.

Dobson Ranch has seven man-made lakes, a city golf course and plenty of mature trees. Those trees are part of the neighborhood's appeal, but they drop leaves into gutters and valleys and can scrape roofs in high wind.
bullets: Trim limbs back from the roof before monsoon season (June 15–September 30).
Clear gutters and valleys of leaves so water drains freely.
After a strong storm, check for lifted shingles, shifted tiles or debris on flat sections.

The joint between an addition and the original roof depends on flashing and careful detailing. On older homes this is a frequent leak point and usually needs to be rebuilt rather than caulked.

Shingles wear faster here than in cooler climates because of UV and heat. Lifespan depends on the product, ventilation and color; an inspection tells you where yours stands.

sections.body:

sections.h2: A tight build window means a shared timeline
sections.body:
Homes in Boulder Mountain were built between 1997 and 2006, a span of about nine years. The oldest are now in their late 20s; the newest are about 20.

Concrete tile is typical for Las Sendas homes of these years, and that is what we expect to find here, though we confirm on each home. Felt underlayment under tile in Arizona often lasts about 20–25 years, so most of the neighborhood is entering the window for a re-felt at roughly the same time. If neighbors on your street have recently had their roofs redone, it is a good prompt to check yours.

Boulder Mountain has a guarded entry. When you call to schedule, tell us how the gate handles contractor visits so our crew is on the list. For a re-felt or replacement, which takes several days and involves material deliveries, the gate may need the dates in advance.

Letting close neighbors know about a multi-day roof project is also a courtesy that helps with parking and deliveries on narrower streets.

Boulder Mountain homes sit in the Usery Mountain foothills with mountain views. Elevated, open lots can take more direct wind during monsoon storms (June 15–September 30), which puts extra stress on ridge caps, hip tiles and roof edges.

View-oriented homes also tend to have more complex roof lines. Each valley and wall transition needs sound flashing. During an inspection or re-felt, these are the areas we look at most closely.

Boulder Mountain falls under Las Sendas HOA architectural review. We did not find specific published roof rules, so contact the Trailhead Office before re-roofing or changing tile color or profile. A re-felt that reinstalls your existing tile usually keeps the appearance the same, but confirm before work begins.

• Repair: for a roof with sound underlayment and a few cracked tiles or a flashing problem. See repairs and maintenance.
  • Lift and relay: new underlayment under your existing tile when the underlayment is worn but the tile is sound.

We explain which option fits after we inspect.

sections.h2: Late-1990s tract homes and their underlayment
sections.body:

Production builders of that era commonly used felt underlayment under tile. In Arizona heat, felt often lasts about 20–25 years before it becomes brittle and starts to crack. On a 1997 home with original underlayment, it is likely at the end of its life, even if the tile on top looks solid.

sections.h2: Signs your Boulder Creek roof is due
sections.body: Failing underlayment tends to show up slowly. Watch for:

Water marks on the attic side of the roof deck
Tiles that have slipped, exposing underlayment
Underlayment at the eaves that looks torn, curled or brittle

sections.body:

Tile from the late 1990s may no longer be made in the exact same profile or color, so we look for the closest match and may move original tiles to the most visible slopes. See tile roofs and our Roofing Cost Guide; every roof is different.

sections.h2: Buying or selling in Boulder Creek
sections.body:
At this age, a roof is a common point of negotiation in a home sale. Buyers should ask whether the roof has been re-felted and, if not, get a dedicated roof inspection during escrow.

Sellers can do the same before listing, so they know what a buyer's inspector will likely find. Either way, written findings make the conversation easier.
Boulder Creek has an HOA. We did not find published roof rules, so ask your association before changing tile color or style. Re-felts that reuse the existing tile generally keep the look unchanged.

Between June 15 and September 30, monsoon storms can bring strong wind and short bursts of heavy rain. Aging underlayment is often first exposed by these storms.

Keep valleys and gutters clear, avoid walking on the tile, and check for broken pieces after big storms. Call us at 602-548-3770, Monday through Friday from 7 am to 5 pm, if you spot a problem.

Still, newer roofs get damaged. Wind lifts tiles, workers crack them, and sealants around vents and flashings can dry out sooner than you would expect in Arizona sun. Small fixes now protect the underlayment, which is the part that keeps water out.

bullets: Cracked tiles from foot traffic during pest control, solar or holiday-light work

sections.body:
Monsoon season runs June 15–September 30. The best time to prepare is late spring.

  1. Clear leaves and debris from valleys and gutters.
  2. Trim tree limbs that hang over the roof.
  3. Once a strong storm passes, scan the yard for tile fragments and the roofline for crooked ridge caps.

If you find damage, our storm damage page explains what happens next.

Mulberry is an HOA community with a clubhouse, pool and courts. We did not find published roof rules, so check with your HOA before any work that changes tile color or style. Like-for-like repairs usually blend in without a problem, and we aim to match your existing tile.

Felt underlayment under tile in Arizona often lasts about 20–25 years, and some newer synthetic products last longer. For a Mulberry home built in 2015–2019, that means underlayment work is likely well into the future.

For now, a roof inspection every few years and prompt repairs after storms are the best way to keep it that way.

sections.h2: What happens on a Mulberry repair visit
sections.body:
When you call about a problem, we ask what you have noticed and when it started. On site, we look at the area of concern from the roof and, when we can, from the attic, then check nearby tiles, flashing and vents for related damage.

We explain what we found in plain terms and give you an estimate before any work begins. On most young roofs the fix comes down to replacing a few tiles, resealing a flashing or swapping a cracked vent boot. Our repairs and maintenance page covers how we handle repairs.

Keep a simple file of roof repairs, inspection reports and any solar or satellite installs. When it is time to sell, a documented roof history answers buyers' questions before they come up. Call us at 602-548-3770, Monday through Friday from 7 am to 5 pm, when you need a repair or inspection.

Every few years, and after any severe monsoon storm. Inspections catch small problems before they reach the underlayment.

Should I walk on my tile roof to check it?

We recommend against it. Concrete tile cracks easily under a misplaced step, and roofs are a fall hazard. Look from the ground or from a ladder at the edge instead, and call us if something looks wrong.

sections.body:
Listing sites use The Groves as a name for part of central-east Mesa. Homes tagged with it fall roughly around Val Vista Drive and Lindsay Road, between Main Street and University Drive, in ZIP codes 85213 and 85205. No source we found publishes exact boundaries, so treat the name as a general area rather than a single community.

Inside that area you will find older single-family streets such as Thayer Estates, which has no HOA, alongside 55+ resort parks including Mesa Spirit RV Resort, Springhaven RV Resort, Citrus Gardens and Las Alegres. Some houses sit on larger lots with RV gates, and Val Vista Drive gives quick access to US-60.

Home listings in The Groves show build years of 1971, 1982, 1984, 1985, 1988 and 1990, and a 1984 Thayer Estates home has a composition shingle roof. A house that old has almost certainly been reroofed at least once, so the question is how old the current roof is, not how old the house is.

Arizona sun is hard on asphalt shingles. Over time the granules wash off, the mat dries out and the tabs curl or crack, and wind lifts the weak ones during summer storms. If your shingles look patchy or you find granules collecting near downspouts, schedule a roof inspection before the next monsoon. Our asphalt shingle page explains the warning signs in more detail.
bullets: Bare or shiny patches where granules are gone
Curled, cupped or cracked shingle tabs
Lifted shingles along ridges and edges after wind
Stains on ceilings below valleys or roof penetrations

sections.body:
Homes of this era often have a low-slope section somewhere: a patio cover, an enclosed porch or a later addition tied into the main roof. Those flat areas hold water longer than the pitched roof and are usually the first place a leak starts.

Depending on what is up there now, a tired flat section can often be repaired, recoated with an elastomeric coating or rebuilt. Where a flat roof joins a shingle roof, the transition flashing deserves a close look too.

sections.h2: Homes in the 55+ RV and manufactured-home parks
sections.body:
The resort parks in The Groves hold park models and manufactured homes, including newer units from builders such as Cavco, Fuqua and Palm Harbor. These roofs are built differently from a site-built house, and many parks have their own rules about exterior work and who can do it.

If you live in one of the parks, check with the park office before any roof work starts. Then give us a call and describe your home and roof; we will tell you honestly whether the job is a good fit for what we do.

sections.h2: Choosing a roof without an HOA
sections.body:
Many streets here, Thayer Estates among them, have no HOA, which means no architectural committee has to approve your shingle color or roof style. That freedom is useful, but it also puts the whole decision on you.

When you replace an older shingle roof, think about color and heat. Lighter, more reflective shingles can help an attic run cooler in a Mesa summer. Ask about ventilation, too, because an attic that cannot breathe shortens shingle life. For a sense of what goes into price, see the Roofing Cost Guide; every roof is different, so a real number needs an on-site estimate.

sections.h2: Storm damage in an older neighborhood
sections.body:
At least one recent listing in The Groves mentions a storm-damaged roof, which is no surprise in an area with older roofs. Arizona's monsoon season runs June 15–September 30, and the outflow winds can peel up aged shingles and drive rain under loose flashing.

After a big storm, walk around the house and look from the ground. Missing shingles, debris on the roof and new ceiling stains are reasons to call. Our damaged roof page covers what to document for an insurance claim.

Missing or lifted shingles, debris on the roof, dented vents and new water stains inside are all good reasons to have it checked. Take photos from the ground before anything is moved.

sections.h2: An older neighborhood near a much older landmark
sections.body:
The Mesa Grande subdivision sits in west-central Mesa, ZIP 85201. One listing gives directions east of Country Club Drive on McLellan Road, south on Grand, then west on Hunter Street. Downtown Mesa is a short drive away.

The name is shared with Mesa Grande Cultural Park, a Hohokam temple mound built around 1100 AD and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978. The mound is ancient; the houses are not, but by Arizona standards they are some of the more seasoned homes you will find.

sections.h2: What a roof on a 1969 house has been through
sections.body:
A verified home in the subdivision was built in 1969 and has a composition roof. After more than 50 Arizona summers, the original roof is long gone, and some homes may be on their third or fourth.

That history can hide problems. Older reroofs sometimes went over existing layers, decking can soften where leaks went unnoticed, and vents or skylights added over the years each bring a new place for water to get in. A careful inspection sorts out what you have before you plan the next roof.
bullets: How many shingle layers are on the roof now
Soft or sagging decking near eaves and valleys
Old pipe jacks and vents that have cracked in the sun
Patched areas that never matched the rest of the roof

sections.h2: Flat roofs on additions and patios
sections.body:
Homes of this era often picked up a family room, an enclosed patio or a carport over the decades, and many of those were framed with a low-slope roof. The seam where an addition meets the original roof is one of the most common leak points in older Mesa homes.

Flat sections can usually be repaired, coated or rebuilt depending on their condition. Our flat roofing page explains the options, and spray foam is worth discussing if you want a seamless surface over an addition.

When it is time to replace, a full tear-off is usually the cleanest choice on an older house because it lets the crew see and repair the decking. It also takes weight off the framing if old layers were left in place.

The verified listing in Mesa Grande has no HOA, so homeowners there can generally choose roofing material and color without association approval. Shingles remain the most common choice for a pitched roof of this style; read about them on our asphalt shingles page. For budget planning, the Roofing Cost Guide lays out what affects price, though every roof is different.

Mesa's monsoon season runs June 15–September 30. Older roofs feel it first: brittle shingles lift, gutters overflow and flat sections pond after a heavy cell passes through.

Spring is the best time to have an older roof checked, while there is still time to fix small issues. If a storm has already done damage, see our damaged roof page for what to photograph and when to call.

On a house from the 1960s, a tear-off is usually the better choice because it exposes the decking for repair and avoids adding weight. We will tell you what we find during the estimate.
Why does my addition leak when the main roof doesn't?
The joint between an addition's flat roof and the original pitched roof is a common weak spot. Flashing there often fails before either roof surface does.
When is the best time to schedule a roof inspection?
Late winter or spring works well, before the June 15 start of monsoon season. That leaves time for repairs before the storms arrive.

sections.h2: Parkwood Ranch at about 25 years old
sections.body:
Parkwood Ranch is a master-planned HOA community in east Mesa, ZIP 85208, made up of numbered parcels and named sub-neighborhoods such as Quinterra at Parkwood Ranch. Richmond American Homes built Quinterra in 2000–2001, and Providence Homes built in Parcel 12, where a verified home dates to 2000. Residents have a playground and biking and walking paths.

Streets such as S Hastings, S Chatsworth, E Carol Ave and E Calypso Ave are lined with homes of the same vintage, which means many roofs here are aging on roughly the same schedule.

sections.h2: Why the tile isn't the problem
sections.body:
A verified Providence Homes listing from 2000 has a concrete tile roof. Concrete tile is durable and can outlast the house, but it is not the waterproof layer. The underlayment beneath it is.

Felt underlayment in Arizona often lasts about 20–25 years before it dries, cracks and stops shedding water. On a home built around 2000, that window is here now. Water can get through a failing underlayment while the tile on top still looks nearly new from the street.

sections.h2: Lift and relay: how underlayment replacement works
sections.body:
When the underlayment is worn out, the usual fix is a lift and relay, sometimes called a re-felt. The crew removes the tile and stacks it, replaces the underlayment and any damaged flashing, then reinstalls the original tile, replacing broken pieces.

Keeping your existing tile saves material and keeps the look the HOA approved originally. You can read more on our tile roofs page. If a lot of tile is broken or you want a different look, a full roof replacement is the other path.
bullets: Tile removed and stacked on the roof
Old felt and worn flashing taken off
New underlayment and flashing installed
Original tile reset, with broken tiles replaced

sections.h2: Signs a Parkwood Ranch roof needs attention
sections.body:
Underlayment failure is often quiet until it is not. Watch for water stains on ceilings near valleys, a musty smell in the attic, or daylight around roof penetrations. Cracked or slipped tiles, often from foot traffic during solar or satellite work, let more sun and water reach the underlayment.

A roof inspection checks the underlayment at the eaves and valleys where trouble shows first, and tells you whether a repair is enough or a re-felt makes more sense.

sections.h2: Working with the Parkwood Ranch HOA
sections.body:
Parkwood Ranch has an HOA, and Quinterra lists its own fees as well. We did not find published roof rules for the community, so check your CC&Rs or call your management company before work starts.

A like-for-like lift and relay usually changes little that the association can see. A new tile profile or color is different and generally calls for architectural approval first. It is easier to ask early than to wait on a decision with the job half done.

Monsoon season runs June 15–September 30, and it is the time an aging underlayment is most likely to show itself. Heavy, wind-driven rain finds every gap.

If you suspect trouble, book an inspection in spring. Cost depends on roof size, tile condition and complexity; the Roofing Cost Guide explains the factors. Financing is available, and you can ask about it during your estimate.

sections.h2: A golf community from the late 1980s
sections.body:
Superstition Springs is a master-planned community in east Mesa, set along US-60 around the Superstition Springs Golf Club. The course opened in 1986, was designed by Greg Nash, and is listed at 6542 E Baseline Rd. Superstition Springs Center mall is close by.

The community includes 8 subdivisions with single-family homes and townhomes, under a master association, the Superstition Springs Community Master Association. Listings appear in ZIPs 85206, 85208 and 85209. Fulton Homes built here, and a verified Fulton home dates to 1995.

sections.h2: Underlayment is the real clock on these roofs
sections.body:
The 1995 Fulton Homes listing has a concrete tile roof. Concrete tile can last for decades, but the felt beneath it often wears out in about 20–25 years in our heat. A roof that went on in the late 1980s or mid-1990s and has never been re-felt is running on borrowed time.

The fix is usually a tile underlayment replacement, also called a lift and relay: the tile comes off, new underlayment and flashing go down, and the tile goes back on. It is a common project in communities of this age.

sections.h2: Living next to a golf course
sections.body:
Homes along fairways deal with a hazard most neighborhoods do not: stray golf balls. A direct hit can crack a concrete tile, and one broken tile lets sun and rain reach the underlayment below it.

If your home backs onto the course, look over the roof from a distance a couple of times a year, especially on the side facing the fairway. A cracked tile is a small repair when it is caught early.
bullets: Cracked or missing tiles on the fairway side
Broken pieces in gutters or on the patio
Stains on ceilings below the damaged area

sections.body:
With a master HOA and 8 subdivisions, roof responsibility may differ between neighborhoods. We did not find published roof rules for the community, and some townhome associations handle roofs on owners' behalf while others leave it to each owner.

Before planning work, read your sub-association's CC&Rs or ask your manager who owns the roof and whether a change in tile color or profile needs approval. Like-for-like work usually moves faster.

sections.h2: What a roof inspection here should cover
sections.body:
On a 30-plus-year-old tile roof, a good inspection goes beyond counting broken tiles. It checks the underlayment at the eaves and valleys, where wear shows up first, along with the condition of flashing at walls, chimneys and skylights.

It should also look at any flat or low-slope areas, such as patio covers, where coatings may be due. The goal is a clear answer: repair now, plan a re-felt soon, or both.

Monsoon season runs June 15–September 30, and the heavy rain tends to expose weak underlayment fast. Many owners in older communities like this schedule inspections in late winter or spring so any re-felt can be finished before the storms.

Costs vary with roof size and tile condition; our Roofing Cost Guide explains the main factors. Financing is available if you ask during the estimate.

Once a year is a sensible habit for a roof this age, and again after any major monsoon storm. Catching slipped or cracked tiles early protects the underlayment.

sections.h2: One neighbor already replaced. Should you?

The 1998 listing has a concrete tile roof that was fully replaced in 2022. That is a useful data point: it shows roofs from the original build are already reaching the end of their first cycle.

It does not mean every roof in Signal Butte Ranch needs a full replacement. In many cases the tile is still sound and only the underlayment beneath it has worn out, which a lift and relay can address. The right answer depends on what an inspection finds on your roof.

sections.h2: Single-story roofs: easier to check, still worth a pro
sections.body:
Single-story homes have one advantage: you can see much of the roof from the yard or a neighbor's driveway. Look for slipped tiles, gaps along the ridge and debris piled in valleys.

What you cannot see from the ground is the underlayment. Felt in Arizona often lasts about 20–25 years, so on a 1998 roof, a roof inspection that lifts a few tiles at the eaves and valleys is the only reliable way to judge it. Please do not walk on concrete tile yourself; it cracks easily underfoot.
bullets: Slipped or cracked tiles visible from the ground
Mortar missing from ridge and hip caps
Leaves and dust packed into valleys
Ceiling stains inside, especially near the edges of the house

sections.body:
A few broken tiles or a single leak point is a repair. Underlayment that is brittle across the roof calls for a re-felt, where the tile is lifted, new underlayment goes down and the same tile is reset.

A full replacement makes sense when many tiles are damaged or you want a new look. If you change the tile color or style, check with the Signal Butte HOA first, since associations usually review visible exterior changes.

Far east Mesa sits close to the Superstition Mountains, and monsoon storms can roll in hard between June 15 and September 30. High wind can shift tiles, and driving rain tests every flashing detail.

After a strong storm, check for displaced tiles and new interior stains. Our storm damage page explains what to photograph before calling your insurer.

sections.h2: Selling soon? Roof condition affects the sale

Buyers and their inspectors pay close attention to roofs on 20-plus-year-old homes. When nearby listings can say "new roof," a home with original underlayment may face more questions.

In a neighborhood full of playgrounds and families, roofs collect more than their share of stray balls and the occasional climb to fetch them. Concrete tile is strong in compression but cracks when stepped on in the wrong spot.

A cracked tile lets UV and water reach the underlayment. If someone has been on the roof, or you spot broken pieces in the yard, a quick repair keeps a small problem from becoming a leak.

Desert Uplands is the name real estate sites use for the foothills of northeast Mesa, ZIP 85207, near the Superstition Mountains and Tonto National Forest. It is an umbrella term, not an HOA. It covers subdivisions such as Las Sendas (including Diamond Point and Stone Canyon), Mountain Bridge, Estates at Desert Shadows, Thunder Mountain Estates, Madrid and Skyview, along with some county-island lots.

Las Sendas is a gated golf community and Mountain Bridge is a gated HOA with a large pool and parks. Other parts are custom homes on lots of roughly 0.5 to 2 acres, some with no HOA at all.

sections.h2: Foam roofs on Territorial and Santa Fe homes
sections.body:
A verified 2005 Las Sendas home in a Territorial style has a foam flat roof. Flat-roofed Santa Fe and Territorial designs are common among custom homes in the foothills, and spray polyurethane foam is a natural fit for them.

Foam's weak point is its coating. The foam itself is protected from UV by an elastomeric topcoat that wears down, and a general rule is to plan a recoat about every 5–10 years depending on exposure and coating type. Recoating on time keeps the foam underneath sound. Read more on our foam roofing page.
bullets: Chalky or thin coating where foam shows through
Blisters or soft spots in the surface
Bird pecks or cracks near parapet walls
Water ponding near scuppers and drains

sections.body:
Pitched tile roofs are common in the area too. A 1998 home without an HOA has a tile roof that received a reflective coating in 2024. Coatings like that are aimed at heat and surface protection, but they do not replace the underlayment underneath.

On a tile roof from the late 1990s, felt underlayment is past the 20–25 years it often lasts here. A tile underlayment replacement is the usual fix when it has worn out.

Las Sendas and Mountain Bridge are gated. When you call to set up an inspection or estimate, tell us how gate access works for your street so the crew can get in without delay.

Each subdivision in the area has its own HOA rules, or none. Check your own association's guidelines before changing roof color or material, and keep in mind that custom homes may have specific design standards.

Big custom homes often combine flat foam sections, pitched tile and parapet walls on a single house, with RV or boat garages adding even more roof area. Every transition between materials is a place where water can sneak in.

An inspection on a home like this should look at each roof type separately and at the joints between them. Cost depends heavily on size and layout; the Roofing Cost Guide explains why every roof is different.

Homes near the mountains catch strong monsoon winds and heavy rain between June 15 and September 30. Flat roofs need clear drains and scuppers before that season starts, and tile roofs need secure ridge caps.

After a storm, check scuppers for debris and look for displaced tiles. Our damaged roof page lists what to document.

Listings show foam flat roofs on custom Territorial-style homes and concrete tile on pitched roofs. Many larger homes combine both.
How often does a foam roof need recoating?
A general guide is every 5–10 years, depending on sun exposure and the coating used. A worn coating leaves the foam exposed to UV damage.
Does a reflective coating on tile replace the underlayment?
No. A coating on tile helps with heat and surface wear, but the underlayment beneath the tile is still what keeps water out and still ages on its own schedule.

Often, yes. Small damage can be patched and the surface recoated, as long as the foam underneath is dry and well bonded.

Is a 2001 tile roof due for underlayment replacement?
It is in the typical window. Felt underlayment often lasts about 20–25 years here, so an inspection will show whether it still has life left.
Can my existing tile be reused?
Usually. In a lift and relay the original tile is removed, new underlayment is installed and the tile is reset, with broken pieces replaced.
What amenities does Mountain View have?
Listings mention a community pool, heated spa, clubhouse, fitness center and playground, with the Hawes trails and Loop 202 nearby.
How do I reach you to schedule?

sections.h2: Getting to know Fountain of the Sun
sections.body:
Fountain of the Sun is an age-restricted 55+ community in east Mesa, ZIP 85208, with a guarded and gated entry and a lake. It has an 18-hole executive golf course with a driving range and pro shop, along with a heated pool and spa, fitness center, pickleball courts, clubhouse, media room and a Veterans Memorial.

Streets include S 80th St, E Pueblo Ave, E Calypso Ave, S Arrowwood Way, S Palo Verde Way and S Boojum Way. A verified home in Parcel No. 2 was built in 1973, with Silvercrest listed as the builder.

Homes from the early 1970s were often built with low-slope roofs rather than steep tile, and in our climate those roofs are typically protected with a reflective coating. A 1973 listing here shows exactly that kind of upkeep, with an elastomeric coating resealed in 2025.

A good elastomeric coating reflects sunlight, keeps the roof surface cooler and seals small gaps. It wears down over time under UV, so recoating on a regular cycle is part of normal ownership.
bullets: Coating that looks chalky, thin or discolored
Cracks or peeling around vents and seams
Ponding water that leaves stains after rain
Interior stains near the edges of the ceiling

sections.h2: Other roof options for a 1970s home
sections.body:
When a low-slope roof is past recoating, there are several directions to go. Spray foam creates a seamless, insulating layer that suits flat and low-slope roofs well. A rebuilt flat roof system is another route.

Homes of this era that have pitched sections may have shingle roofs, which can be replaced with new asphalt shingles. An inspection is the way to learn what is on your home now and which option fits it.

Because the entry is guarded, call ahead and let us know how the gate handles contractors. Many guard-gated communities need the resident to add a visitor's name in advance.

The community has an HOA. We did not find published roof rules, so check with the association about any color or material standards before choosing a new coating or roof system.

Roof decisions in a 55+ community often involve adult children or other family members, sometimes from out of state. We are glad to walk through findings with whoever you would like to include, on the phone or at the house.

We will explain what we saw, what is urgent and what can wait, and give you a written estimate to review together. Financing is available if you ask during your estimate.

Low-slope roofs drain more slowly than steep ones, so clogged drains or worn coating can turn a monsoon downpour into a leak. Monsoon season runs June 15–September 30.

A spring roof inspection catches thin coating and blocked drains while there is still time to fix them. For a sense of cost drivers, see the Roofing Cost Guide.

faqs: Is Fountain of the Sun a 55+ community?
Yes. It is an age-restricted 55+ community in east Mesa, ZIP 85208, with a guarded and gated entry, a lake and an 18-hole executive golf course.
When were homes in Fountain of the Sun built?
A verified home in Parcel No. 2 was built in 1973, with Silvercrest listed as the builder. The community's homes date to the 1970s.
Why do so many Fountain of the Sun roofs have coatings?
Homes of that era often have low-slope roofs, and a reflective elastomeric coating protects them from UV and heat. One 1973 home here had its coating resealed in 2025.
How often should a roof coating be redone?
It depends on the product and sun exposure. Signs it is time include chalking, thinning, cracking and peeling, and an inspection will tell you how much life is left.
Can my low-slope roof be converted to foam?
In many cases, yes. Spray foam works well on flat and low-slope roofs and adds insulation, but the existing roof has to be evaluated first.
How do I get a roofer past the guard gate?
Let us know your gate procedure when you call. Most guard-gated communities need the resident to add the contractor's name to the visitor list ahead of time.
Can my son or daughter join the roof walk-through?
Absolutely. We are happy to go over findings with family members in person or by phone so everyone understands the options.
Do you work on the golf course or common buildings?
Common-area buildings are handled through the HOA. If the association is looking for a roofer, its manager can call us directly.
How do I contact you?
Call 602-548-3770, weekdays 7 am to 5 pm. When we're out on a roof and can't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

sections.h2: A Mesa address on county land
sections.body:
Dreamland Villa is not inside Mesa city limits. It is an unincorporated island of Maricopa County surrounded by Mesa, and homes use Mesa mailing addresses in ZIP 85205. Most of the time residents never notice the difference.

Roofing can be one of the exceptions. Because the land is under county jurisdiction, building permits for roof work may be handled by Maricopa County rather than the City of Mesa. Please confirm the current requirements with the county before a project begins, and ask any roofer you talk to how they plan to handle it.

Ground was broken in 1958 and Dreamland Villa opened in January 1959, developed by Joe and Ross Farnsworth of Farnsworth Construction Co. The first section covered 200 acres near Main Street and 54th Street. Later sections continued into the early 1970s, and the community grew to 18 sections and more than 5,000 residents.

The Dreamland Villa Community Club, at 320 N 55th Pl, is voluntary. Members enjoy Read Hall, Farnsworth Hall, swimming pools, a Desert Nature Walk and a Memory Brick Garden.

A verified Dreamland Villa home from 1965 has a composition roof. Ranch homes of this era commonly pair a low-pitch shingle roof with flat or low-slope sections over carports, patios and Arizona rooms added later.

After 60-plus years, these homes have been reroofed several times. Watch for multiple shingle layers, tired decking and patched-together flat sections. Our shingle page and flat roofing page explain the common fixes.
bullets: Shingles curling or losing granules
Flat sections with cracks, blisters or ponding
Leaks where a carport or Arizona room joins the house
Soft spots that suggest damaged decking

sections.body:
The community club is voluntary, and the research we found shows no mandatory HOA roof rules. That means homeowners can usually pick roofing material and color without association approval.

It also means nobody else is tracking your roof's age. Keep your own record of when the roof was last replaced or coated, and plan for a roof inspection every few years.

sections.h2: Making roof decisions as a 55+ homeowner
sections.body:
Many Dreamland Villa residents like to include family in a roofing decision. We are happy to walk the property with you and anyone you want there, or to explain our findings to family by phone.

You will get a written estimate that spells out the work. If you are weighing cost, the Roofing Cost Guide explains what drives price, and financing is available on request during your estimate.

Monsoon season, June 15–September 30, is hardest on older roofs. Brittle shingles blow loose and flat sections over carports pond after a downpour.

If a storm leaves debris on the roof or a new stain on the ceiling, call for a look before the next one. Our damaged roof page explains what to photograph first.

faqs: Is Dreamland Villa part of the City of Mesa?

On a home this old, a full tear-off is usually best. It removes extra weight and lets the crew inspect and repair the decking underneath.

Yes. We are glad to meet with you and your family at the house or to go over findings with them by phone.

Ring our Gilbert office at 602-548-3770 on weekdays from 7 am to 5 pm, and if we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

Apache Wells is an active-adult 55+ community in northeast Mesa, ZIP 85215. Streets such as N Middlecoff Dr, N Nicklaus Dr and N Stockton Pl take their names from golf. Related Sunrise Village sits at 5830 E McKellips Rd.

sections.h2: Many home types, many roof types
sections.body:
Apache Wells includes site-built homes, mobile homes, condos at the Village at Apache Wells, and townhomes. Verified listings show a 1976 home in Unit 4b, a 2003 home in Sunrise Village and a custom infill home on the course from 2024.

That spread means roof ages and styles vary a lot. The 1976 home has a composition roof that was replaced in 2019. Older homes here commonly combine shingle and low-slope roofs, while mobile homes have manufactured-home roofs of their own design.

sections.h2: Condo owners: check with the HOA first
sections.body:
In the Alta Mesa condominiums at the Village at Apache Wells, a listing states that the HOA fee covers roof replacement. If you own a condo there, contact the association before hiring a roofer, because the roof may not be yours to replace.

Townhome and single-family owners should also read their documents. Responsibility can differ by section, and the community HOA may have standards for exterior changes.

sections.h2: Care for older shingle and low-slope roofs
sections.body:
On 1970s homes, shingle roofs that are 10 or more years old should be watched for granule loss and curling, and flat sections over patios and carports for cracks and ponding. A shingle roof replaced in the late 2010s, like the 2019 reroof noted above, still benefits from a periodic look.

Low-slope sections can often be extended with an elastomeric coating or converted to spray foam. Pitched sections are a job for new shingles when the old ones are done.
bullets: Granules collecting in gutters or at downspouts
Coating worn thin on flat patio roofs
Cracked rubber boots around plumbing vents
Water marks on ceilings near exterior walls

sections.body:
Homes along the fairways can take an occasional golf ball hit. Shingles usually shrug it off, but a strike can crack a vent cap or skylight, and on a tile roof it can break a tile.

If you hear a hit, look over the roof from the ground afterward. Our repair and maintenance page covers the small fixes that keep a roof sound.

Many Apache Wells residents involve family when deciding on a roof. We will walk the roof findings through with you and with anyone you would like, on site or on the phone, and leave a written estimate to review.

Monsoon season runs June 15–September 30, so spring is a good time for a roof inspection. The Roofing Cost Guide explains what affects price, and financing is available.

sections.h2: Golf balls, lakes and summer storms
sections.body:
Homes on golf lots see stray balls, and a hard strike can crack a vent cap or knock granules loose. Lakeside lots catch wind across open water during monsoon storms, which run June 15–September 30.

After a strong storm, look for lifted shingles and debris. Our damaged roof page covers what to record for insurance, and the Roofing Cost Guide explains replacement cost factors, though every roof is different.

Curling, cracking, missing shingles and heavy granule loss are the main signs. An inspection gives you a clear answer and an idea of remaining life.

neighborhoods.answer: Integrity Roofing replaces tile underlayment, repairs leaks and inspects roofs in Rancho del Mar, ZIP 85210, near Baseline Road and Country Club Drive. Homes here were built in 1993–1994 with concrete tile, so original felt underlayment is now past 30 years old, well beyond the 20–25 years it often lasts in Arizona.

facts.location: West-central Mesa near Baseline Rd and Country Club Dr
facts.type: Single-family subdivision; the verified listing states no HOA

sections.body:
Rancho del Mar is a single-family subdivision in west-central Mesa, ZIP 85210, built in 1993–1994. It sits near Baseline Road and Country Club Drive, close to Rancho Del Mar Park, Costco and US-60. Streets include W Mendoza Ave, W Nopal Ave, W Natal Cir and W Madero Ave.

Homes range from about 1,338 to 3,765 square feet, many of them large two-story family houses, some with pools. Continental is listed as the builder on a Unit 2 home from 1994.

The verified 1994 home has a concrete tile roof. If a Rancho del Mar roof has never had its underlayment replaced, that layer is now more than 30 years old, which is past the 20–25 years felt commonly lasts here.

Old felt dries out and cracks, especially near the eaves and in valleys where water concentrates. Leaks may start small and show up only after the heaviest monsoon rains, which makes them easy to ignore until the ceiling drywall is damaged.

sections.h2: How we handle a re-felt on a two-story home
sections.body:
On a lift and relay, we remove the tile, install new underlayment and flashing, and reset the same tile, replacing any broken pieces. On a two-story home, the upper roof and any lower roof sections over porches or garages are all part of the job.

Two-story houses add steeper access and more careful tile staging, which affects time and cost. The tile roof page explains the process, and the Roofing Cost Guide covers what drives price.
bullets: Upper and lower roof sections both inspected
Valleys and wall flashings replaced where worn
Pipe and vent flashings renewed
Original tile reset; broken tile replaced

sections.body:
The verified listing in Rancho del Mar states there is no HOA. Without an association, you can generally choose to keep your current tile or switch to a different tile or color without architectural review.

If you are planning a full roof replacement rather than a re-felt, it is worth comparing tile profiles and colors while you have the chance. Lighter colors can reflect more heat.

Backyards with pools often come with palms and other trees, and their debris ends up in roof valleys and gutters. Packed valleys slow drainage and push water under tile.

A yearly maintenance visit to clear valleys, reset slipped tiles and check flashings helps the underlayment last. It is especially worthwhile before monsoon season, June 15–September 30.

sections.h2: Selling or buying in Rancho del Mar
sections.body:
A buyer's inspector will note the age of a 1990s tile roof. Knowing ahead of time whether the underlayment has been replaced, and having the paperwork to show it, makes negotiations simpler.

If you are buying, ask the sellers when the roof was last re-felted. If no one knows, a roof inspection can give you a clearer picture before closing.

Where is Rancho del Mar?

If the underlayment has never been replaced, it is over 30 years old and likely past its useful life. An inspection will confirm its condition.

Without an HOA, you generally have the freedom to choose. During a re-felt, most owners keep their original tile, but a full replacement opens up new options.

Check the seller's disclosure or any receipts from previous owners. If there is no record, an inspection that lifts a few tiles will show the underlayment's age and condition.
How do I get an estimate for my Rancho del Mar home?
Call 602-548-3770, Monday through Friday from 7 am to 5 pm. Leave a message if we're unavailable, and we'll return your call within 24 hours.

sections.h2: The Mesa Santa Rita Ranch, not the Tucson one
sections.body:
Search for Santa Rita Ranch and most results point to a much larger master-planned community in Vail, near Tucson. This page is about the small Santa Rita Ranch subdivision in Mesa, ZIP 85212, near Guadalupe Road and Signal Butte Road. Streets include S Del Rancho Ave and S Del Rancho Cir.

The Mesa subdivision has its own association, which covers grounds maintenance. Homes enjoy Superstition Mountain views and are close to parks, golf and freeway access.

A verified home in Parcel 8 was built in 2000 by Hacienda Builders and has a concrete tile roof. Tile on a home that age is often still in good shape, but the felt underlayment beneath it tends to last about 20–25 years in Arizona.

That makes now a sensible time to find out where your roof stands. An inspection that checks the underlayment at the eaves and valleys will tell you whether you have years left or should plan a re-felt.

Some Santa Rita Ranch lots have RV gates and 3-car garages, and wider garages mean more roof area and more valleys where the garage roof ties into the house. Those valleys carry a lot of water during heavy rain and are often the first place underlayment wears through.

Look for stains on the garage ceiling or along interior walls near the garage. They can be early signs of a valley leak that is worth a repair before it spreads.
bullets: Garage ceiling stains near the house wall
Cracked or slipped tiles in valleys
Debris packed where two roof planes meet
Rusted or bent flashing at wall transitions

sections.body:
When underlayment is worn out, we lift the tile, take off the old felt and worn flashing, install new underlayment and flashing, and reset the original tile. Broken tiles are replaced as needed. Many people call it a re-felt or a lift and relay.

Reusing your tile keeps the home's look the same, which helps with the HOA. If you want a new tile style or color instead, see our roof replacement page and check with the association before you commit.

Southeast Mesa sees strong monsoon storms between June 15 and September 30. Wind can shift tiles near ridges and edges, and heavy rain exposes worn underlayment quickly.

A spring check gives you time to fix what is found. If a storm has already caused damage, our damaged roof page explains what to do first. Cost varies by roof, and the Roofing Cost Guide outlines the factors.

faqs: Is this the Santa Rita Ranch near Tucson?

No. This page covers the small Santa Rita Ranch subdivision in Mesa, ZIP 85212, near Guadalupe Road and Signal Butte Road. The larger, better-known Santa Rita Ranch is in Vail, near Tucson, outside our service area.
Who built Santa Rita Ranch in Mesa?
Hacienda Builders is listed as the builder of a verified Parcel 8 home, built in 2000.
What roof do Santa Rita Ranch homes have?
The verified 2000 home has a concrete tile roof, the standard choice for east Mesa homes built around that time.
Is my 2000-era tile roof due for work?
Most likely, since felt underlayment often lasts about 20–25 years in Arizona. An inspection will tell you whether it needs replacing soon.
Does the Santa Rita Ranch HOA cover roofs?
Listings say the association covers grounds maintenance. Nothing we found says it covers roofs, so treat the roof as the owner's responsibility unless your CC&Rs say otherwise.
Do I need HOA approval for roof work?
Like-for-like repairs and re-felts using the same tile usually raise few questions. A new tile color or style generally needs approval, so check with the association first.
Why does my garage ceiling have a stain?
On homes with large garages, the valley where the garage roof meets the house is a common leak point. Have it inspected before the damage spreads.
Can I keep my existing tile when the underlayment is replaced?
Yes, in most cases. The tile is lifted, new underlayment goes down and the same tile is reset, with broken pieces replaced.
How do I schedule an inspection in Santa Rita Ranch?
Reach us at 602-548-3770 on weekdays, 7 am to 5 pm. If we don't answer, leave your name and number and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
